meta.source: Eskom/NTCSA Generation Connection Capacity Assessment (GCCA 2025, published Oct 2023), with Western Cape and Eastern Cape reflecting the congestion-curtailment capacity NERSA actually APPROVED on 29 Apr 2025 (4% cap, in force 1 Apr 2025 - 31 Mar 2028): 1,180 MW WC and 400 MW EC. Not the 3,470 MW originally proposed in the Jan 2024 GCCA Addendum, which NERSA did not grant in full.
meta.replaces: Headroom previously derived from this app's own corridor-utilisation search, which only knew about OPERATIONAL plant. It therefore ignored the committed-but-unbuilt pipeline (REIPPPP preferred bidders through BW6, plus private wheeling projects holding budget quotes) - exactly what depleted the Cape provinces in reality. That made it badly optimistic: 72,250 MW national solar headroom against a published 19,940 MW, and thousands of MW shown as available in the four supply areas Eskom reports as zero.
meta.caveat: The six non-Cape figures date from Oct 2023 and have very likely been drawn down since - NTCSA's own project dashboard (Nov 2025) shows 15.2 GW of solar alone seeking connection. Treat them as an upper bound. NTCSA published a GCCA 2025 Curtailment Update on 31 Oct 2025 that should be checked for revised numbers.
meta.note: GCCA capacity is technology-agnostic - it is connection capacity at transmission substations, not a per-technology allowance - so the same regional figure applies to every technology and allocations draw from one shared regional pool.
